reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Distal radius ORIF in a 72 y with severe idiopathic PAH and RV failure (TAPSE 1.4, RVSP 72, 6MWD falling) whose ambrisentan has not been given for 3 days because pharmacy has not verified her home supply; a supraclavicular block is requested, which will likely block the phrenic nerve, and she desaturated to 84% after 0.5 mg midazolam in 2024.

asa.rationale: WHO FC III pulmonary arterial hypertension with severe RV dysfunction, home oxygen.

decision.recommendation: delay a few hours to restart ambrisentan and change the block
decision.rationale: PAH therapy must never be interrupted; give ambrisentan now and involve the PH team. Choose a block that spares the diaphragm (infraclavicular or axillary) with minimal sedation.

redFlags.evidence: Ambrisentan not given 10/25 and 10/26 (awaiting pharmacy verification); PH team: never interrupt therapy.
redFlags.action: Escalate to pharmacy and PH team, give ambrisentan before surgery.

redFlags.implication: Hypoxemia and hypercarbia raise PVR and can precipitate RV failure.
redFlags.action: Infraclavicular or axillary brachial plexus block instead.

redFlags.evidence: TAPSE 1.4, D shaped septum, RVSP 72, JVD, edema, BP 96/58, NT-proBNP 1,980.
redFlags.implication: Systemic hypotension causes RV ischemia and spiral collapse.
redFlags.action: Arterial line, norepinephrine or vasopressin ready, avoid fluid boluses, keep sinus rhythm, inhaled pulmonary vasodilator available.

redFlags.evidence: SpO2 84% after midazolam 0.5 mg in 2024; oxycodone at 0400.
redFlags.action: Minimal or no sedation, ETCO2 monitoring, oxygen.

planItems.item: Infraclavicular or axillary block with minimal sedation
Norepinephrine and vasopressin available; inhaled pulmonary vasodilator available
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
